newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria cabinet approves c.bank law amendments.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria cabinet approves c.bank law amendments.

text.p: Bulgaria's cabinet approved on Thursday a package of legal amendments which restructure the central bank under the requirements of the new currency board, Justice Minister Mladen Cherveniakov said.
"Under the amendments Bulgaria retains its central bank as an institution. The bank's operation will be restricted in line with the currency board rules," Cherveniakov told reporters.
The International Monetary Fund proposed a restrictive fixed exchange rate regime to restore confidence in the crumbling financial system and curb inflation.
The currency board system is expected to be introduced in the first quarter to halt further economic collapse and provide access to external funding, much needed for foreign debt payemnts.
An IMF mission is due to arrive shortly after parliament approves a new Socialist cabinet by mid-January. The mission will be expected to negotiate the introduction of the system.

Under the amendments, which must now gain parliamentary approval, the central bank will no longer set the daily currency fixing nor the central interest rate. It will be banned from open market operations and from trading government securities.
Under the currency board system, levs in circulation must be matched by foreign exchange reserves. The interest rate will be determined by the interbank market.
The bank will not fund the government and commercial banks.
During the first three months of the system's operation, considered a transition period, the government will have access to central bank lending for up to six-month loans, said Cherveniakov.
Under the bill commercial banks will rely only on collateralised lending from the central bank to avoid short-term liquidity problems.

The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) will be reduced to four departments -- an Issue Department, which supervises the currency board implementation, a Banking department, a Bank Supervision Department and a Debt Management unit.

Parliament and the president are expected to appoint a new seven-member executive board for a five-year term, said Cherveniakov. The board will consist of a governor, three deputies and three experts, who are not involved in any financial institutions or the government administration.
Parliament is expected to decide to which currency, the dollar or the mark, to peg the lev. The lev will remain the official payment currency inside the country, said Cherveniakov.
